items.title: ASA Pushes Back on Insurer Claims That the No Surprises Act IDR Process Is Broken
items.reason: The item addresses disputes over the Independent Dispute Resolution (IDR) process implementation under the No Surprises Act, directly covering enforcement and operational issues central to the law's administration.
items.summary: The American Surgical Association (ASA) has responded to insurance industry arguments that the No Surprises Act's Independent Dispute Resolution (IDR) process is malfunctioning, challenging insurer claims about the process. This dispute reflects ongoing tension over how the IDR mechanism—a core component of the No Surprises Act designed to resolve billing disputes between providers and insurers—operates in practice. The exchange is significant for revenue-cycle teams because the IDR process directly impacts how out-of-network billing disputes are resolved and whether balance-billing protections are effectively enforced. The disagreement between provider and insurer stakeholders over IDR functionality may influence future regulatory adjustments or litigation related to the No Surprises Act's implementation.
